entry.shape: { v: string, i: I18n, x: ComviHandle }
entry.v: core library version that produced the entry
entry.i: the exposed i18n instance (its 13 members; no instanceId — removed in 0.8, R3-14 H1)
entry.x: the handle an in-context editor drives the instance through; see `handle`

coreToPage.description: An instance announces itself only through the devtools() plugin (`createI18n({ plugins: [devtools()] })`, `@comvi/core/devtools`); a bare instance never touches the global. In a browser, setup pushes ONE entry; without a window (SSR) nothing happens. 0.8 is the thin hook of R3-15: core makes no probe of the global's shape, mints no id and keeps no page-level slot.
coreToPage.expose: window.__COMVI__ ||= []; then window.__COMVI__.push(entry). Core calls nothing on the global but push here.
coreToPage.removal: destroy() runs q.splice(q.indexOf(entry) >>> 0, 1) on window.__COMVI__ as it is then: the SAME entry object, and nothing when it is not found (-1 >>> 0 is past the end). Core calls nothing on the global but indexOf and splice here.
coreToPage.guards: exposure and removal are wrapped in try/catch: a global that is not an array, or one that throws, never breaks construction or destroy (the entry is then simply not exposed or not removed).
coreToPage.removedIn08: Moved out of core by R3-15 (owner 27.10): the v1 legacy registry (register/unregister), the push/remove hook probes and their order, the `comvi-<n>` counter with its `Symbol.for("comvi.core.instanceCounter")` slot, `instanceId` and its idempotence, and the editor-loader slot `Symbol.for("comvi.devtools.editorLoader")` with its load key. Tests for each moved duty belong to lot 8 (extension/editor), listed in .lot1-pending-tests.md.

pageToExtension.description: The consumer (in-context editor / Chrome extension) drains window.__COMVI__ on boot. To observe later instances and their removal it may replace the global with an ARRAY whose own push, indexOf and splice it controls — the only three members core 0.8 ever calls; that is the whole of what protocol 2 asks of a consumer. Lot 8 rewrites the consumer side (hook shape, marker rule, id assignment) on this protocol; until then `consumer07` describes the 0.7 consumers.

consumer07.note: The 0.7 consumers' own hook, kept for reference until lot 8 rewrites it. NOT part of protocol 2: core 0.8 never reads hookShape, the marker or requiredMembers, and lot 8 must not treat them as v2 requirements.
consumer07.hookShape: Object.assign([], { __comviEditorHook: true, push, indexOf, splice, instances, get, version }) — an array, so `||= []` keeps it, with OWN push (a new entry), indexOf and splice (an entry's removal) shadowing Array.prototype.
consumer07.markerRule: The hook carries `__comviEditorHook === true` so that whichever consumer installs first (in-context editor or extension detector) is REUSED by the other instead of swapping again. It is not proof of a hook: it is page-writable, and a page that pollutes Object.prototype.__comviEditorHook marks every object. A consumer MUST therefore validate requiredMembers before adopting a marked global, MUST probe Array.isArray BEFORE the marker (so a polluted prototype cannot make a raw queue array look like an installed hook), and MUST read the marker and the entry's `i` as OWN properties rather than with `in`. A marked global that fails requiredMembers is treated as whatever it otherwise looks like — a v1 legacy registry if it duck-types as one, else a truthy non-conforming global: left untouched, never adopted, never read, and never a thrown error.

pageToExtension.idCollisions: 0.8 entries carry no id. The editor assigns an internal `inst` per instance when it builds its marking closure (editor plan §3.2: empty when the page has one instance, `comvi-<n>` when it has several) and re-marks through x.mark when a second instance appears.

versionPairing.core-0.8+extension-0.6.x: UNSUPPORTED — the released extension looks for the 0.7 editor-loader slot and reports `no-loader`. Release gate (R3-15): the extension that speaks protocol 2 is published to the Chrome Web Store before @comvi/core 0.8 is published to npm.
versionPairing.core-0.7+extension-for-0.8: the extension's own business (lot 8 decides whether it keeps a 0.7 path)
versionPairing.two-cores-0.8-same-page: both push onto the one array; each removes only its own entry object

handle.shape: { p: 2, kind: 'comvi', read(ns, locale), state(), mark(fn | null), load(version?) } — exactly these six own members
handle.p: 2 — the handle protocol. An editor picks its driver by p + kind and refuses a protocol it does not support.
handle.kind: 'comvi' for @comvi/core. A driver for another library brings its own kind; an editor that meets a kind it does not know raises a TYPED error (editor side, lot 8) and never guesses.
handle.read(ns, locale): the messages of the pair as the catalogs hold them — keys to ICU source text, the messages add()ed on top included; no markers ever; {} for a pair that holds nothing. A list and a preview: the value to edit comes from the platform (editor plan §3.6).
handle.state(): a fresh object on every call (compare `rev`, never identity): the instance's published State (@comvi/core/internal) with the namespaces it needed added as `ns`. Protocol 2 guarantees ONLY the fields in `stateFields` for its whole lifetime; every other field of State is internal (no semver guarantee) and an editor must not read it.

stateFields.rev: number; moves on every published change
stateFields.locale: string; the current locale as the app spells it
stateFields.c: namespace → locale → slot; a slot's `m` (base) and optional `p` (patch on top) are flat key → ICU source maps. read(ns, locale) is the merged view of one pair and the preferred way to read it
stateFields.ld: string[]; loads in flight, each the locale, a NUL character, then the namespace
stateFields.ns: string[]; the namespaces the instance needed — pinned by the `namespaces` option, held by a component or load()ed; one joining publishes, none is removed (lot 4c) — loaded, still loading, failed or with no catalog alike (the editor refreshes loaded locales × ns from the platform)

handle.mark(fn | null): sets the marking hook State.mk = fn ((out, key, ns) => out) and PUBLISHES a new state; a value that is not a function clears it like null (an editor bug never makes the host's t() throw), so every binding re-renders marked; null clears it and publishes again. translate() calls the hook for found and missing keys (the `missing` output), with the namespace looked up; a call with { markers: false } (or <T markers={false}>) never reaches it — the opt-out is checked BEFORE the hook. view() inherits it. Messages already compiled stay compiled across mark on/off and add() (H3). The only way a state gets a hook: an instance without devtools() is never marked.
handle.load(version?): resolves, with the editor global (window.ComviInContextEditor), once that global is available. `version` is an exact SemVer 2.0 version without build metadata (1.2.3, 1.2.3-rc.1; no leading zeros, no empty, `_` or leading-zero numeric prerelease identifiers) or 'latest' (the default), read once as a string; anything else — a URL, a path, a query — REJECTS with a TypeError and creates nothing. Today core resolves it by inserting <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@comvi/editor@<version>/dist/standalone.iife.js"> (host and path are core constants); the contract is the resolved global, not the script, so a bundled editor can satisfy it later without a protocol change (R3-16). Rejects with an Error when the script fails (`[@comvi/core/devtools] load failed`) or runs without leaving the global (`… no editor`); a bad version rejects with a TypeError. NEVER throws synchronously: a Trusted Types refusal of the src assignment, or a page without a document element, is a rejection. No cache, no timeout, no retry, no CSP diagnostics, no cache salt: a second call loads again; the extension owns dedupe (skip when the global exists), its CSP listener (installed before calling load), its timeout and the exact version it passes (R3-15).
handle.afterDestroy: the entry is gone from the queue; mark() does nothing (no new state, t() of the destroyed instance stays unmarked), read() and state() return the last state, and load() still only loads the editor.
